Commission Spring assessment finds France non-compliant (5.5% of 2026 deficit estimate), prompting Macron to demand a PLFR and rating agencies to signal negative outlooks; Banque de France notes markets orderly despite 138bp spread. history.narrative: The Cour des comptes spring report revised the 2027 trajectory to 5.5% of GDP (worse than government's 5.0%), but rating agencies held fire pending scheduled reviews, and no downgrade materialised. The government tabled the PLFR before the first round, while Macron's call for a pre-election vote went unheeded as the Assembly suspended plenary sittings until after 18 April. RN amplified deficit/49.3 framing; the NFP confirmed a single candidacy. Markets stayed tense but orderly (spread ~138-145bp).

history.narrative: The first round proceeded on 18 April as constitutionally confirmed, with the Conseil constitutionnel receiving tallies normally. Fiscal pressure intensified rather than eased: the Cour des comptes' certified 5.5% 2027 deficit estimate, the Commission's non-compliant EDP stance and rating agencies' explicit incorporation of the worse figures kept the OAT-Bund spread near 145bp, though markets stayed orderly. Macron's post-election push to bring the PLFR to a vote within a month met a deferred but not hostile Assembly, leaving resolution to the post-election session. INSEE confirmed definitive 2026 accounts for 30 April.
